PRENATAL GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Patient ID: [redacted ID]
Referring Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Date of Collection: [redacted date]
Date of Report: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Maternal Age: 36 years
Gestational Age: 10 weeks
Indication for Testing: Advanced maternal age, prenatal screening for common trisomies
Sample Type: Chorionic villi (uncultured)
Procedure: Chorionic villus sampling (CVS)

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR) for rapid aneuploidy detection

METHODOLOGY
DNA was extracted from uncultured chorionic villi. QF-PCR analysis was performed using fluorescently labeled primers for short tandem repeat (STR) markers on chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. The following markers were analyzed:
- Chromosome 13: D13S631, D13S258, D13S742, D13S628
- Chromosome 18: D18S535, D18S391, D18S390, D18S386
- Chromosome 21: D21S1435, D21S1411, D21S1412, D21S1437

Peak area ratios were calculated for each informative marker. Normal diallelic patterns indicate two copies of each chromosome.

RESULTS

Chromosome 13: NORMAL COMPLEMENT
All informative markers showed normal diallelic patterns
Peak ratios within normal range (1:1 to 1:1.5)

Chromosome 18: NORMAL COMPLEMENT
All informative markers showed normal diallelic patterns
Peak ratios within normal range (1:1 to 1:1.5)

Chromosome 21: NORMAL COMPLEMENT
All informative markers showed normal diallelic patterns
Peak ratios within normal range (1:1 to 1:1.5)

CONCLUSION
No evidence of trisomy 13, 18, or 21 detected by QF-PCR analysis.

LIMITATIONS
This test screens only for trisomies of chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. It does not detect:
- Other chromosomal abnormalities
- Balanced rearrangements
- Mosaicism below 20%
- Single gene disorders
- Maternal cell contamination cannot be excluded without additional testing

RECOMMENDATIONS
Full karyotype analysis from cultured chorionic villi is recommended to follow this rapid screening test. This will provide comprehensive chromosomal analysis and exclude other chromosomal abnormalities not detected by QF-PCR.

This report has been reviewed and authorized by:
[redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Director, Prenatal Genetics Laboratory
[redacted date]
